thread:
ops-bot: ALERT: Canary deployment `canary-v12` crossed p99 latency SLO (SLO=200ms). p95=320ms, p99=1.8s, streaming stalls observed. Auto-escalation triggered. :rotating_light:
ryan (oncall): oncall here, looking. Which stack? any customer impact yet?
anya (sre): I see a spike in the canary fleet in us-east-1. Tail latency jumps around 18:14 UTC. No error-rate increase, just huge tail on streaming responses (ws frame timing).
sami (eng-runtime): adding context: v12 introduced KV cache persistence change + async KV flush. Might impact tail when cache miss + cold KV fetch during streaming.
clara (product): are any paying customers routed to canary? I thought it's 5% traffic shadowing for a subset of orgs. Need to assess impact quickly for compliance customers.
ryan (oncall): @clara we have 100% shadow for internal test orgs and 3% live traffic for a small enterprise pilot (org-582). Paging pagerduty for the pilot.
pagerduty-bot: pagerduty: Incident PD-8773 created and assigned to #incidents with severity=high. Notifying oncall schedule.
anya (sre): quick traces: most inflated spans are in `stream_writer.py:emit_chunk` waiting on `kv.get` (latency 600-1500ms on tail). Backend GPU inference latency unchanged. Looks like blocking IO inside streaming path.
sami (eng-runtime): confirmed. Here's a quick repro log from a canary node:
```
[14:15:22] INFO stream start session=abc123
[14:15:22] WARN kv: miss, fetching from remote (lat=842ms)
[14:15:23] INFO emit_chunk duration=1150ms
```
ryan (oncall): current mitigation plan? Can we route canary traffic to v11 while we triage?
sami (eng-runtime): yes. Recommend shifting the 3% live traffic for org-582 back to stable v11, keep shadowing for metrics. I can run traffic-shift now.
anya (sre): Also temporarily increase streaming timeouts to avoid connection stalls causing client retries. Set `stream_chunk_timeout_ms` from 1500 -> 4000 for the canary route.
clara (product): notify the pilot customer proactively (account owner) that we're routing them to stable due to a perf regression; they should see lower latency. I'll draft a short note.
ryan (oncall): @sami go ahead with the shift. Runbook step: `infra route shift --from canary-v12 --to v11 --percent 3 --org org-582`
sami (eng-runtime): running command now. output:
```
> infra route shift --from canary-v12 --to v11 --percent 3 --org org-582
shifting traffic... ok (3% -> v11)
verification: healthy
```
anya (sre): verified infra metrics — the canary p99 for us-east-1 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms after shift for live traffic. Shadow metrics still show the regression, so root cause stays in v12 code path.
ryan (oncall): good. escalate to eng-runtime for rollback decision. Sami, can you roll back canary entirely (kill pods / promote previous image) if needed?
sami (eng-runtime): I can do full rollback but want to capture logs/config diffs first. I'll snapshot config and then rollback. Snapshot done. Rolling back canary set to v11 now.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollback started for canary-v12 -> v11 by sami at 14:23 UTC.
clara (product): I've messaged the pilot account and internal CS: "We've routed your traffic to the stable model for lower latency while we investigate. No action needed on your side"
anya (sre): after rollback p99 across the board returned to ~210ms within two minutes. Streaming stalls gone in canary nodes too.
ryan (oncall): creating an incident doc w/ timeline and owner. Owner: sami for RCA, anya for mitigation & monitoring, ryan for incident comms.
ryan (oncall): next steps: full RCA, check KV persistence change in v12, run targeted load test with cold cache to reproduce, and code patch to async IO path.
anya (sre): assigning follow-ups in Jira: INF-1298 (RCA), INF-1299 (fix + test), INF-1300 (improve canary gating).
clara (product): will follow up with customer update after RCA.
ops-bot: INCIDENT: PD-8773 marked RESOLVED by ryan at 14:31 UTC (reason: rollback to v11 restored SLO). :white_check_mark:
ryan (oncall): handing off to oncall tomorrow for postmortem follow-up. If anything regresses, re-open PD. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
